h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא, ט׳ Ki Seitzei, 9
Welcoming the Seven Shepherds to the Shabbos Meal

p: who are called "shoshvinin," the attendants of the wedding,
(Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma, end of Parshas Eikev; Devarim Rabbah 3:16, Tanchuma Eikev 10):
"Moshe is the attendant of the King;
Aharon is the attendant of the Queen."
For the aspect of Moshe Rabbeinu
is that he brought the Torah down from Heaven,
is to bring words of Torah
"and brings them near to the Torah."
וְשַׁבָּת אִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב רד, א)
And regarding Shabbos, it says in the holy Zohar (II 204a):
the Shin is the secret of the three Avos
who are united with the only daughter,
and she is crowned with them."
And the Musaf of Shabbos is reckoned
as corresponding to the holiness of Yosef HaTzaddik,
And this is what we say beforehand:
correspond to the holiness of the three Avos.
of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
the first meal as corresponding to him.
And the attribute of Yitzchak is the dread
וְאִיתָא בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג)
And it says in Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu (beginning of chapter 3; Seder Eliyahu Rabbah 3:1):
in accepting the yoke of His kingship, may His Name be blessed,
corresponds to the attribute of Malchus, as is known.
And the attribute of Yitzchak, which is dread,
is a level greater than fear;
for fear is only that a person pictures
that the King of the kings of kings,
the Holy One, Blessed is He, stands over him;
when he stands before the King in actuality,
so that of itself there falls upon him
the dread that is upon those who are near.
And the greater a person's fear,
the greater his joy as well;
and this is "much joy shall come,"
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
for corresponding to him the holy Arizal reckoned
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham,"
the two thousand years of Torah,
are from the side of the right,
are from the side of the left,
and together they are three hundred and ten";
and 207 is the numerical value of "or," light.
And it says (Zohar II 167a, and in the Tikkunim):
'and there was light' — this is the left."
for on the side of the right
compared with the side of the left,
and on the side of the right 207
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham."
הוּא כְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
who is the essence of the blessings,
and handed it over to a tenant, etc.;
גִּלָּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יִצְחָק
the Holy One, Blessed is He, revealed Himself to Yitzchak
because of the tree of deadly poison,
And so it is in Rashi's commentary on the Chumash (Bereishis 25:11).
"'Through Yitzchak' — and not all of Yitzchak."
It turns out that the essence of the blessings of the Avos
And the expression "and abundant blessings" is used
the holiness of Yosef as well,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא פִּנְחָס רמב, ב)
as they said (Ra'aya Mehemna, Pinchas, Zohar III 242b):
"Body and covenant we reckon as one";
are bound one to the other";
and peace is the attribute of Yosef HaTzaddik,
And Yosef is the channel of blessings,
as appears from the words of the holy Zohar,
מְבוֹרָךְ כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אָמֵר (בְּרֵאשִׁית מט, כב)
And corresponding to the holiness of Yaakov and Yosef
And with all three there is said
the joy, the light and the blessing,
And there is also said of them
meaning that they come of themselves,
since Shabbos is crowned with the Avos,
and Yaakov and Yosef we reckon as one.
for in every meal there is something
which is meant for Moshe and Aharon,
who are a chariot for the attributes of Netzach and Hod.
the time when the Written Torah is bestowed,
that all agree the Torah was given on Shabbos,
and also the time when there is bestowed
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א מז, ב)
and the Written Torah and the Oral Torah
are the holiness of Moshe and Aharon
nevertheless, since the essence of their holiness
Moshe, the attendant of the King,
to bring the words of Torah down from Heaven,
and Aharon, the attendant of the Queen,
to bring the words of Torah
to invite them to the meal,
so that their holiness shine forth;
for the main bestowal of words of Torah
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
as they said in the holy Zohar (II 88a):
the head of Ze'eir Anpin is filled
with the dew of the Holy Ancient One,
and it pours it into the Field of Apples
take delight at these three times."
and does not say when that time is,
when Yisrael eats the Shabbos meal,
the dew of the Holy Ancient One
and fills the head of Ze'eir Anpin.
And the dew of the Ancient One
alludes to the dew of Torah,
as has been explained many times.
And this is why we invite the attendants
this too is an abundance of kinds,
just as with all the holinesses there is mentioned
the holiness of all seven attributes
and "bas" is the attribute of Malchus,
and David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
is a chariot for this attribute.
For at the Shabbos meals one merits
the holiness of all seven attributes
